 :JUDGMENT:
The Petitioner has filed the Petition against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained him in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 18.01.2022 at about 7.30 p.m. the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on the Motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-44-X-8541 which was riding by one Nanda Kumar K., on Turuvekere-Tiptur Road at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and when they reached near Shivananda's land, Somenahalli Village, the rider due to high speed, lost control over the vehicle and fell down into the left side ditch, thereby the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, Petitioner was shifted to Hemavathi Hospital, Tiptur,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing Agriculture and milk vending and was earning more than Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

3. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motorcycle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

sentences.text: Despite of service of notice, Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
In response to the notice, Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
It contended that, no other person was injured in the said alleged accident and the person who is stated to be a rider of the motorcycle did not sustained any injuries.
Hence, it is clear that the petitioner himself was riding the motorcycle, skid and fell down into the ditch from the motorcycle and sustained injuries.
Further it admits the issuance of insurance with respect to motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-44-X-8541 in question in favor of respondent No.1 insured and the same was valid at the time of accident.

Further it contended that the owner of the vehicle has willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not had a valid and effective driving license to ride the motorcycle on the date of accident.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
5. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 18.01.2022 at about 7.30 p.m., near Shivananda land, Turuvekere-Tiptur road,
Somenahalli Village, Tumakuru in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Splendor motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-X- 8511?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents at Ex.P1 to 14.
He further got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.15 to 20.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any evidence.
7. I have heard the arguments, perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

8. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order,

Issue No.1:-
It is the case of the Petitioner that he has sustained injuries in the accident caused by the rider of the offending Motor cycle bearing No.KA-44-X-8541.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and its specific contention is that the petitioner himself was riding the offending bike, skid and fell down.
Hence tort- feaser can not claim benefit out of his own negligence.

Ex. P.6
the Wound Certificate, shows that petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

12. Further, P.W.1 examined the Medical Record Officer of Hemavathi Hospital, Tiptur, as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.15 to 18 i.e., authorization letter, True copy of MLC Register Extract, True copy of Police intimation copy and Case sheet.
They show that on the date of accident i.e.,18.01.2022 itself the petitioner was admitted in the hospital and treated for the injuries sustained in the RTA.
The Ex.P.16 MLC register extract clearly shows the history as "H/o alleged RTA on18.01.2022 at 7.30 p.m. near Somenahalli pt is a pillion rider.

He is travelling in a splender bike & fell down &
sustained injury to the rt thigh and left clavical."
This document made it clear that the petitioner was pillion rider of the bike.
Further PW.1 got examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as P.W.3 and got marked Ex.P.19 and 20 i.e., Clinical notes and X-ray.

sentences.text: The above said FIR shows that the accident was taken place on 18.01.2022 and the complaint was lodged on 22.01.2022.
Hence there is 4 days delay in lodging the complaint.
14. At this juncture it is profitable to refer the judgment reported in 2011 AIR SCW 1530 between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and others.

entities.text: 2011 AIR SCW 1530 between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein Hon'ble Apex Court held that:
"20. It is well - settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case
Knowing the Indian condition as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the police station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the police station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with police.
Delay in lodging FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justify to the victim.
In case of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If courts find that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent person then, even if there is delay in lodging FIR the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
15. In the case on hand there is 4 days delay in lodging the complaint.
The accident had taken place on 18.01.2022 and the complaint was lodged on 22.01.2022.

Wherein, the complainant who is the relative of the petitioner explained for the delay in lodging complaint that he could not file a complaint because he was with the petitioner in the hospital, hence the delay was caused.
The explanation given by the complainant for the delay is acceptable one.
As held in the case of Ravi (supra) delay in lodging FIR would not be fatal and claim petition need not be dismissed on that ground.
16. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination P.W.1 he specifically denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 that himself riding the bike and skid and fell down.
Nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
17. Though the Respondent No.2 has taken contention that the petitioner himself was riding the bike and fell down, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Moreover, as discussed a above the petitioner was got admitted in the hospital immediately after the accident on the same day and given history before the doctors that he was the pillion rider.
The MLC register extract makes it clear that the petitioner was the pillion rider of the offending bike.
Hence, there is no grounds to disbelieve the version of the petition.
Further more after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge-sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle and the said charge sheet has not been challenged by the rider.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and due to the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in Manjunatha vs Sandeep K.P on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127486368/
5 the "Affirmative".

sentences.text: 18. Issue No. 2 - As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 47 years.
He has produced Aadhar card and PAN card marked at Ex.P.10 and 11 to prove his age.
As per aadhar card and PAN card, his date of birth is shown as 06.07.1975.
The accident has taken place on 18.01.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 47 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
20. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was an agriculturist and milk vendor and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove avocation and income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
22.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-6 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. There is an abrasion over the right thigh 2.
There is shortenings of right thigh, abnormal mobility, tenderness over the right thigh X-ray shows # Rt Femur 3.
There is abnormal mobility over the left shoulder, X-ray shows # Left Clavicle.
wherein, the Doctor has opined that the injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 and 3 are grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.3 has also re-iterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
23.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

Manjunatha vs Sandeep K.P on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127486368/
6
III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
24. The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 18.01.2022 and discharged on 24.01.2022 at Hemavathi Hospital, Tiptur.
25. Upon going through the Discharge summary at Ex.P.9 which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 18.01.2022 to 24.01.2022 at Hemavathi Hospital, Tiptur i.e., for 6 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 6 days.
26. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, at least it took two months for recovery.
I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence,
the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/- under this head (@ Rs.15,500/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.

V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
28.
The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical expenses.
He has produced 2 medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.70,458/-.
I have gone through the medical bills.
There is no serious dispute on the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills totally amounting to Rs.70,458/-, which is rounded up at Rs.70,500/- Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.70,500/- as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

29. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he cannot lift or hold weight from his left hand, cannot raise his left hand above shoulder level, restrictions of movements, cannot do any manual work involving stand or walk without support, cannot sit with cross legs, cannot use Indian toilet, cannot climb stairs and cannot squat.
30.

Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as P.W.3 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination Manjunatha vs Sandeep K.P on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127486368/
7 he made.
Further, he got marked Clinical notes and X-ray at Ex.P.19 and 20.
He assessed total disability of the Right Lower Limb at 47% and disability of the Left Arm at 27% and whole body physical disability at 23%.
31. In the cross-examination, PW.3 has admitted that the femur fracture is an un-displaced and middle 1/3 fracture and closed fracture.
Further admitted that only nailing has been done.
Further he admitted that as the injury is closed fracture, there is no loss of tissue as there is development of cells.
Further he admitted that conservative treatment was given as a result of the fracture was simple in nature.
Further admitted that in follow up treatment the doctor has advised only for femur fracture and not for clavicle injury.
Further he admitted that femur fracture is united.
32. The Doctor has assessed total disability of the Right Lower Limb at 47% and disability of the Left Arm at 27% and whole body physical disability at 23%.

Upon careful consideration of the assessment of disability made by PW.3 keeping in mind the fact that PW.1 personally appeared before this court and deposed, also keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 and the treatment which he has taken, Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed appears to be at the higher rate.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 18% would be just and proper.
33. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 13.

With multiplier of 13, income of Rs.15,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 18%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,35,240/- (Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 13 x 18/100 =Rs.4,35,240/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,35,240/- under this head.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
34.
The doctor i.e., PW.3 has deposed that the Petitioner needs another surgery for removal of the implant which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation.
A perusal of recent X-rays marked at Ex.P.20
, it shows that implants are in-istu.
Those implants to be removed.
Hence, by considering the future medical expenses for removal of implant, it would be proper to grant Rs.25,000/- as a compensation under this head.

In MFA.1749/2023 (MV-D) between The Divisional Manager, KSRTC Vs. Mahadevaiah.M and another, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held as follows:
"15.3 We are in the complete agreement with the above decisions.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the amount due under the head loss of future prospects is yet to become due, it would be illogical and illegal to direct the insurance company to pay interest on loss of future prospects.

Manjunatha vs Sandeep K.P on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127486368/
8
Therefore, out of the total compensation payable, the respondent is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation under the head loss of future prospects.

However,
so far as the remaining compensation, is concerned, respondent is liable to pay interest."
In view of the said dictum, the amount awarded under the head future medical expenses does not carry any interest.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
35.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 70,500/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 31,000/-
laid up period 6.

Loss of Future earnings Rs.4,35,240/-
7. Loss of Future medical Rs. 25,000/-
expenses Total Rs.6,34,740/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,34,740/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

36. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-X-8541.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.

There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
37. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

9 ORDER

The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/Sec.
166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled to Compensation of Rs.6,34,740/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E-payment, after his proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

The explanation given by the complainant for the delay is acceptable one.
As held in the case of Ravi (supra) delay in lodging FIR would not be fatal and claim petition need not be dismissed on that ground.
17. Though the Respondent No.2 has taken contention that the petitioner himself was riding the bike and fell down, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Hence, there is no grounds to disbelieve the version of the petition.
Further more after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge-sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle and the said charge sheet has not been challenged by the rider.
Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and due to the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
19. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 47 years.
He has produced Aadhar card and PAN card marked at Ex.P.10 and 11 to prove his age.
The accident has taken place on 18.01.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 47 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove avocation and income.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 18% would be just and proper.
In MFA.1749/2023 (MV-D) between The Divisional Manager, KSRTC Vs. Mahadevaiah.M and another, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held as follows:
"15.3 We are in the complete agreement with the above decisions.
In view of the said dictum, the amount awarded under the head future medical expenses does not carry any interest.
